# ⚡ Kubernetes Command of the Day (2026-08-09)

## 📌 Retrieve Previous Container Logs Before Crash

```bash
kubectl logs <pod-name> --previous
```

| Metadata | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Category** | `Troubleshooting` |
| **Difficulty** | `Beginner` |
| **Safety Rating** | **🟢 Safe** |
| **Verification Status** | Unverified ⚠️ (Tested against Kubernetes local environment.) |

---

### 📖 What It Does

Fetches stdout/stderr logs from the container instance immediately preceding a crash or restart.

### 💡 Why It Is Useful

Essential for diagnosing CrashLoopBackOff root causes when current container logs are empty.

### 💻 Practical Example

```bash
kubectl logs web-backend-7945d8b857-x492l -c app --previous
```

### ⚙️ Prerequisites

Requires active `kubectl` connection and appropriate cluster permissions.

### ⚠️ Common Mistake

Running against the wrong namespace or context without checking current-context first.
